source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: A Thing Model (TM) is a JSON-LD 1.1 document conforming to [WoT-TM 1.1][WoT-TM-1.1]. It describes an abstract class of Things and typically omits `href` values from its forms. Thing Models are reusable: a concrete Thing Description MAY extend or compose one or more Thing Models through WoT `tm:extends` and `tm:ref` mechanisms or JSON-LD `@type` declarations.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: Although both document classes use JSON-LD and share part of its vocabulary, a WoT Registry MUST treat them as distinct Resource types. Their intended use, validation rules and lifecycles differ.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's `forms` array describes protocol bindings that MAY also be represented as `endpoint` Resources. See [Section 6.3](#63-thing-description-to-endpoint-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's property/action/event data schemas (declared inline via WoT data-schema vocabulary) MAY reference external schemas managed by the xRegistry Schema Registry. See [Section 6.4](#64-thing-description-to-schema-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description MAY reference one or more Thing Models from which it is derived. See [Section 6.1](#61-thing-description-to-thing-model).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: This specification does not require the Registry to resolve or validate these cross-references. An implementation MAY check that a referent exists, but it still stores and serves the document when a referent is absent. A Consumer composing a TD from Thing Models or binding an affordance to an endpoint depends on those references independently of the Registry's checks.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Version of a `thingdescription` or `thingmodel` Resource holds a complete WoT document, stored without rewriting its bytes. A Resource's `wotid` and registry Resource id are stable across compatible revisions. `wotid` is declared with [`matchversions`][xRegistry matchversions]. A registry MUST reject a Version that supplies a different `wotid`. A Thing Model's major version MUST be part of its `wotid`. A breaking change MUST use a new `wotid` and a new Resource ([Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Thing Model Resources and Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] `true`. Core orders each Resource's [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage by SemVer precedence and forbids multiple roots with these aspects. The assignment rules for the corresponding authored fields are:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TM | `version.model` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TD | `version.instance` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For either Resource type, the registry MUST inspect the authored field without modifying the stored document. The original authored field MUST NOT be rewritten, including when absent or non-SemVer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A valid authored value is SemVer 2.0.0 without build metadata and fits Core's 128-character [id constraint][Core id constraints]. SemVer build metadata (`+build`) MUST be rejected as `invalid-version`, since `+` is not allowed by Core's id constraints. An authored SemVer value that exceeds Core's 128-character id limit MUST also be rejected under those constraints.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: `N` is the lowest positive integer whose complete id is not already used in the Resource. The registry MUST assign an omitted `versionid`. A supplied `versionid` MUST equal the authored or generated assignment, or the registry MUST reject it as `version-mismatch`. A supplied id that violates Core's id grammar MUST be rejected as `invalid-version` before this comparison. Core requires an immutable, unique [`versionid`][Core versionid]. This extension defines the assignment in place of its default [Version ID algorithm][Core Version IDs].

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The Registry MUST perform assignment and creation atomically with respect to concurrent writes, so two writes cannot claim the same generated id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Thing Model Version and each Thing Description Version MUST have a server-set, read-only `versionorigin`. Its value MUST be `authored` when the Version's id comes from a SemVer authored field, and `generated` otherwise.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Client-supplied `versionorigin` MUST be ignored under Core's [read-only attribute rules][Core read-only rules]. The model initializes the attribute to `authored`. When the registry assigns a generated id, it MUST replace that initial value with `generated`. The model default does not replace the assignment rules above.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Generated ids are prereleases. They MUST NOT be used as minimum-version floors, even when the target Version is absent.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For Thing Models, the Resource-level [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute in `meta` MUST default to `backward`. A backward-compatible TM revision MUST NOT remove or narrow an affordance, a data schema or an `@type`, and MUST NOT introduce a new mandatory member. Narrowing includes reducing the accepted values or operations of an existing member. These constraints apply to every earlier Version in the Resource's Core [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A Registry MAY validate this domain-specific compatibility rule through Core's [`validatecompatibility`][Core validatecompatibility] capability. Core's [`strictvalidation`][Core strictvalidation] rules still apply. Absence of a domain validator does not permit a Producer to publish an incompatible revision under the same `wotid`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: When [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is false, Core's SemVer [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] orders the default. A late `1.0.1` after `1.1.0` MUST NOT replace `1.1.0` as the default. A sticky default MUST be honoured.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For migration, an operator SHOULD inventory every Version and root of a legacy Resource before enabling this model. Compatible TM roots SHOULD be imported into one SemVer-ordered lineage with ids assigned by the rules above. Incompatible roots MUST be placed in distinct Resources with distinct major-version `wotid`s.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator SHOULD inventory legacy TD Resources with manually assigned `versionid`s and re-import them with ids assigned from `version.instance` or generated by these rules.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Where changing an old immutable id or authored document would be necessary, the operator SHOULD preserve the legacy Resource outside the conforming collection and import a copy under a new registry Resource id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator MUST preserve authored bytes, record old-to-new registry paths for callers holding pins, and establish a valid default before enabling `singleversionroot`. An operator MUST NOT claim that an unresolved multiple-root Resource conforms to this model.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.4. Document Store

requirements.text: An xRegistry-unaware WoT consumer MAY use a Version's `self` URL with the `$details` suffix removed, or its `shortself` URL, as a regular WoT TD or TM URL. The unchanged `self` URL returns xRegistry metadata rather than the document. The metadata and document URLs are not interchangeable.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined, and server-known extension, attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Thing Description

requirements.text: The TD's `version.instance` carries its revision, including breaking major revisions. A major revision remains under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. If a Resource declares the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all its Versions MUST adhere to that policy. A TD that identifies a different Thing MUST use that Thing's `id` and a corresponding Resource. See [Section 1.3](#13-versioning).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.3. WoT Identifier

requirements.text: A WoT identifier is held in the `wotid` attribute. It is distinct from the xRegistry `thingdescriptionid`/`thingmodelid`, which identifies the Resource within a Registry. The two MAY hold the same string when the authored identifier satisfies xRegistry's id grammar. Most do not: a URL such as `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a legal xRegistry id. The model therefore keeps them as separate attributes rather than reusing the Resource id. [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids) defines how the two relate.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification MAY include additional extension attributes, including the `*` attribute of type `any`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.1. Thing Description Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Description (the `thingdescription` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Description Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] value `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] value `true`, as specified in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning). Core derives `ancestorid` by SemVer precedence and enforces one root ([`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid]).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The Version-level `versionorigin` attribute is REQUIRED, read-only, and uses the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`. The `versionid` is assigned from `version.instance` when that member is SemVer without build metadata. Otherwise it is the lowest free `0.0.0-N` id. The original document bytes, including `version.instance`, are not rewritten.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingdescription` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`. [model.json](model.json) declares the `format` enumeration as `strict`, so a registry rejects any other value rather than merely discouraging it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `contenttype` of a `thingdescription` document MUST be `application/td+json` per [WoT-TD 1.1 §12.1][WoT-TD-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: `contenttype` is client-supplied and determines the media type used to serve the stored bytes through the document view ([Section 1.4](#14-document-store)). A Registry MUST NOT serve a stored document under a client-supplied media type that would interpret it as active content, such as `text/html`, `image/svg+xml` or `application/xhtml+xml`. A Registry MUST either reject such a write or serve the document under the media type this section requires.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: WoT tooling dereferences a Version's document-view URL directly. For documents it did not author, a Registry SHOULD additionally return `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` or serve them from an origin separate from any Registry user interface. See [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, distinct from the `thingdescriptionid`. See [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids). The OPTIONAL `derivedfrom` attribute lists the `wotid`s of the Thing Models this Thing Description extends or composes. It is a producer-supplied index rather than an authority over the document's own references, as [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) describes.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: All Versions of a single Thing Description Resource MUST adhere to the semantic rules of the Thing Description's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute, if specified.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification SHOULD use the xRegistry default algorithm for generating new `versionid` values.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The default Version is the one served when no Version is named. It MUST be determined by the xRegistry Core rules, including the Resource's [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] setting. A deployment MAY use that setting to pin the default to a Version other than the newest. This specification does not redefine default-Version selection. See [Version IDs][xRegistry version-ids] for more information.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.3. Thing Model Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Model (i.e. the `thingmodel` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Model Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingmodel` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`, enforced by the same `strict` enumeration used for `thingdescription`. The `contenttype` MUST be `application/tm+json` per [WoT-TM 1.1 §12.2][WoT-TM-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents, and the same constraint on serving stored bytes as active content applies as in [Section 4.2](#42-thing-description-resources).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `compatibility`, `versionid`, `versionorigin` and [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] rules for Thing Models are defined in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning), subject to Core's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] and [`versionid`][Core versionid] semantics. The Version-level `versionorigin` is a REQUIRED string with the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`, and is read-only. The model declares `compatibility` under `metaattributes`, with `required: true` and `default: backward`, as Core requires for an attribute with a default.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED on a `thingmodel` and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, which is distinct from the `thingmodelid`. Where a Thing Model extends another via a `tm:extends` link relation, or references one via `tm:ref`, or composes one via `tm:submodel`, the referenced Thing Models' `wotid`s SHOULD be listed in `derivedfrom`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - A URI-reference pointing to a TD MAY use a JSON-Pointer ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901)) fragment to deep-link into a particular property, action, or event affordance, e.g. `…/thingdescriptions/lamp-42#/properties/status`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.2. WoT Thing Model

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1` and the document's top-level `@type` MUST include `tm:ThingModel`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: Tools and autonomous agents need explicit metadata to choose among documents describing similar Things rather than inferring their provenance from titles or naming conventions. Both `thingdescription` and `thingmodel` Resources carry the following OPTIONAL attributes:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer choosing between candidate Thing Models SHOULD prefer, in order:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: If the choice remains open, the Consumer SHOULD prefer the document whose `canonicalurl` it already trusts. [model.json](model.json) declares the `maturity` enumeration as `strict`, so a Registry rejects values outside this set. A Consumer that nonetheless encounters one, for example from a federated Registry, MUST NOT rank it above `Experimental`. This specification defines no precedence for it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are advisory and unverified assertions by the Resource's writer about the document's origin and maturity. This specification defines no mechanism for a Registry to validate a `publisher` or `standardsbody` claim. A Registry MUST NOT be assumed to have validated one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer MUST NOT treat these attributes as authenticated provenance. The preference order only breaks ties among documents the Consumer already trusts, whether by Group, writer identity or an out-of-band signature. It MUST NOT be used to establish trust in a document from an untrusted writer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: One `wotid` MAY legitimately match several Resources written by different parties ([Section 5.3](#53-lookup)), so a Consumer can face this choice. See also [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are also not part of a document's semantic identity. A registry MUST NOT treat two documents as the same document because their provenance attributes agree, nor as different documents because they differ: identity is `wotid` alone ([Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: These identifiers serve a similar purpose but follow different grammars. `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a valid entity id or `xid` component. An `xid` is not what a Thing author writes. Where an authored identifier satisfies the id grammar, a client MAY use it as the Resource id. A Registry cannot rely on that choice.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A deployment MAY derive its Resource ids from `wotid` values by a convention of its own. The [OpenUSD Artifact Registry][OpenUSD Draft] working draft defines one such construction. No convention is mandated by this specification, and a Consumer MUST NOT assume that an id it did not assign was produced by one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` MUST NOT encode a compatible revision of the document it names. A Thing Model's major version MUST be included in that stable identity, for example `urn:fabrikam:lamp:v1` or `https://fabrikam.example/tm/lamp/v1`. Minor and patch revisions are carried by `versionid` and `version.model`, not appended to the identifier. No particular spelling of the major-version token is mandated.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: When a document is revised compatibly, its `wotid` and Resource id MUST remain unchanged, and a new Version is created under the same Resource. A Thing Model breaking revision uses a distinct major-version `wotid` as specified in [Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers). A Thing Description major revision remains under its existing `id` and `wotid`. A new TD identifier names a different concrete Thing.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` is REQUIRED, and the rule for populating it depends on the document:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries an `id` member, `wotid` MUST equal it verbatim. A registry that parses the stored document MUST reject a write whose `wotid` differs from that `id`, rather than storing two identities for one document. A registry that does not parse the document cannot detect the disagreement. Both types of registry MUST NOT rewrite either value to resolve the disagreement, because [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) forbids editing the document.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries no `id` member — which [WoT-TD 1.1][WoT-TD-1.1] permits for TDs served from a fixed URL, and which is common for TMs — the Producer MUST supply a `wotid` at write time, and that supplied value is thereafter the document's identity in this registry.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - A registry MUST reject a write that supplies neither an `id` member nor a `wotid`, rather than inventing one, because an invented identifier is not stable across registries.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: A breaking Thing Model change MUST use a new major-version `wotid` and a distinct Resource. The predecessor's `wotid` MUST NOT be modified. A major Thing Description revision remains a Version of the same concrete Thing under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. A distinct TD `id` and `wotid` identify a different concrete Thing, not a breaking revision of the existing one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: The predecessor Resource MUST be marked with Core's [`deprecated`][xRegistry deprecated] attribute, whose `alternative` MUST be the successor Resource's URL. Its Versions MUST remain retrievable. Deprecation alone MUST NOT cause the resolver to redirect a reference to the successor. A Consumer MAY inspect the successor and explicitly choose to adopt its different identity.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST store the WoT document byte-for-byte as supplied, apart from transformations the client explicitly requested.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST NOT rewrite the document's `id` member, its `links[].href` values, its `tm:extends` or `tm:ref` targets, or any other identifier internal to the document, into registry-specific identifiers.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A retrieval of a stored Version through the document view MUST return the exact bytes supplied, as the xRegistry Core document view already requires. Re-serializing the document — reordering members, re-indenting, or normalizing its JSON-LD — is not permitted.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: `derivedfrom` is a producer-supplied *index* of the document's references, not an authority over them. A registry MAY verify that it matches the `tm:extends`, `tm:submodel`, `tm:ref` and `links[].rel="type"` targets in the stored document, and SHOULD reject a write where the two disagree. Where a registry does not verify, the document is authoritative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: When making a trust, allow-list or compliance decision about a document's lineage, a Consumer MUST derive that lineage from the document itself and MUST NOT rely on `derivedfrom` alone.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: An implementation SHOULD serve this query in time that does not grow with collection size, in practice by indexing `wotid` on both `thingdescriptions` and `thingmodels`. A linear scan for each reference would make TD composition slower as the collection grows.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A `wotid` SHOULD be unique within a Group, so that a Group-scoped query for one identifies a single Resource. Across Groups a `wotid` MAY repeat — the same vendor TM legitimately appears in two tenants' Groups. A registry-wide query MAY therefore match more than one Resource. A caller that needs exactly one narrows the query by naming the Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A Registry-wide query MUST return every matching Resource rather than an arbitrary one of them. [Section 4.6](#46-provenance-and-selection-metadata) governs how a Consumer chooses among them.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A request to the Resource URL without a Version returns the Core default, even when [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is true. A registry MUST serve that default when no Version is named.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: For WoT document reference resolution, a resolver MUST use [Section 5.4](#54-versioned-reference-resolution), not lexical id order, publication time or an assumption that the default satisfies the reference.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: Callers SHOULD NOT fold the identifier and version into one opaque string. When carrying both through a transport, such as message headers, a caller SHOULD use separate values, for example a `wotid` header and a `versionid` header, rather than a single compound token like `urn:fabrikam:lamp@3` that every recipient has to take apart. The identifier stays a WoT identifier, and the version stays a `versionid` the recipient can put straight into a URL.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The CloudEvents WoT profile is proposed. A CloudEvent using this profile MUST carry Thing identity in the `source` URI-reference using the query parameters below. The profile does not prescribe the URI scheme or the rest of the URI-reference. The `source` MUST conform to CloudEvents Core; it MAY be relative, although Core recommends an absolute URI. A fragment, including an empty fragment, is permitted. This profile does not assign it a meaning.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The `wotid` query parameter carries the Thing's WoT identifier. When present, `wotversion` carries an exact xRegistry `versionid`, not a minimum-version floor or the TD's `version.model`. The `wotid` parameter MUST precede the OPTIONAL `wotversion` parameter, separated by `;`. Other query parameters MAY follow the standardized parameters. This profile does not assign them a meaning; a publication contract MAY define their semantics. A Consumer MUST NOT reject a `source` solely because it contains additional query parameters.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The standardized parameter names are case-sensitive and MUST appear literally. Each MUST use `name=value` with a non-empty value. `wotid` MUST appear exactly once; `wotversion` MUST NOT appear more than once. A Producer MUST place `wotid` first and, when present, `wotversion` immediately after it. Additional parameters MUST follow them.

review.note: The public query parser checks literal case-sensitive names, required nonempty values, duplicates and standardized parameter ordering. The encoder emits wotid first and optional wotversion second. Additional parameters remain uninterpreted; full CloudEvents URI and TD-view processing are separate obligations.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: For standardized values, a Producer MUST use UTF-8 percent encoding with uppercase hexadecimal digits. RFC 3986 `unreserved` characters and `!$'()*,:@/?` MUST remain unescaped. `%`, `;`, `=`, `&`, `+` and `#` within a standardized value MUST be percent-encoded. A Producer MUST NOT use form-query encoding or encode a space as `+` for these values. These encoding requirements do not apply to additional parameters.

review.note: The public encoder preserves all declared unreserved and permitted punctuation characters and encodes reserved delimiters, percent, space and Unicode using uppercase UTF-8 percent escapes. Parsing leaves additional parameters untouched.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: A Consumer MUST split the query at `;` before decoding the standardized values. It MUST reject a missing or empty `wotid`, an empty `wotversion`, a duplicate standardized parameter, or a standardized parameter in the wrong position. For a standardized value, it MUST reject an invalid percent escape, invalid UTF-8, or an unescaped character outside the permitted set. It MUST percent-decode each standardized value exactly once and MUST NOT interpret `+` as a space. These validation rules do not apply to additional parameters.

review.note: The public parser splits at semicolons before exactly one strict UTF-8 percent decode. It rejects invalid escapes, invalid UTF-8, missing/empty/duplicate/misplaced standardized parameters and forbidden raw characters, including plus. Additional parameter values do not acquire these standardized-value checks.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: A configured resolver MUST select exactly one Thing Description Resource whose `wotid` equals the decoded identifier within its configured scope. A missing match MUST produce `not-found`; ambiguous matches MUST produce an error rather than selecting an arbitrary Resource. Group-scoped lookup and uniqueness follow [Section 5.3](#53-lookup).

review.note: AcquireCloudEventSourceAsync implements exact identity lookup in one caller-authorized TD Resource collection, with complete Version metadata, missing-match and ambiguity errors, captured model/context checks and finite budgets. DirectoryMapping supplies a public acquired-byte workflow. This remains partial configured-resolver evidence: authored URI/base/context processing and alias provider integration are not implemented by this acquisition API. No resolved TD view or native qualification is claimed.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: When `wotversion` is present, the resolver MUST select that exact Version or fail as `not-found`. When it is absent, the resolver MUST select the Resource's current Core default Version, including a sticky default, or fail as `not-found` if no default is available. It MUST NOT apply the floor or prerelease selection of Section 5.4 to this CloudEvents source selection. References within the selected TD still follow their applicable resolution rules. The unversioned source can therefore resolve to a different view after the default changes.

review.note: AcquireCloudEventSourceAsync selects the exact decoded Version or captured Core default, including lower, sticky and prerelease defaults. Exact selection does not require an available default, does not apply ordinary SemVer or incremental floors, and fails as not-found without fallback. Core Version lookup remains case-sensitive. Repeated acquisition observes a changed default without changing retained bytes or an explicit Version selection. The block remains pending because references within the selected TD still require authored-reference provider integration and resolved-view composition; source acquisition alone does not implement that obligation.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: For this profile, an explicit `wotversion` MUST identify a stable logical resolved TD view. A Producer MUST create a new publication Version of the selected Thing Description Resource when that view changes, including when its source closure changes. The new Version MUST follow [Section 1.3](#13-versioning), including assignment from an authored SemVer `version.instance` or the generated-id rules. A Producer MUST NOT reuse an authored instance version for a changed published view. This requirement applies to publication Versions used by this profile; it does not make all xRegistry Versions immutable or change Core's general update semantics.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The resolved TD is the result of applying the applicable WoT resolution rules to the selected sources. Producing or publishing that result MUST NOT overwrite or rewrite stored authored source bytes ([Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The CloudEvents `subject` MUST address the resolved TD, not an unresolved source document. It MUST be an RFC 6901 URI-fragment JSON Pointer, with `#` addressing the whole resolved TD. For example, `#/events/overheated` addresses that event affordance in the resolved view. A Consumer MUST apply the pointer only after obtaining that view and MUST report failure if the pointer does not identify a value.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: A Consumer MAY retrieve the published resolved TD or reconstruct the same logical view from a complete pinned source closure and the applicable resolution rules. If the closure cannot establish that result, the Consumer MUST obtain the published view or report failure. It MUST NOT substitute live dependencies or a pointer into an unresolved source document. [Section 5.4.4](#544-publication-closure) records unresolved closure mappings; the existing closure extension and schema alone do not establish that such reconstruction is possible.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: The CloudEvents `type` identifies the event's payload contract, not the Registry Resource or TD Version. The [CloudEvents WoT profile's type rules](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/a9b0cde4368d25189d97b5557141ed5795a1a10a/cloudevents/extensions/wot.md#type) define its dot-separated symbol and revision. Its final segment MUST be `vN`, where `N` is a positive decimal integer without leading zeros. The publication profile MUST assign the same revision to the same payload contract. A Producer MUST use a new revision when a member is added or removed, a member's type or meaning changes, or the payload envelope changes, even when the change is backwardly compatible.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup / 5.3.1. CloudEvents WoT Source Resolution

requirements.text: Changing an individual value or the presence of an already OPTIONAL member does not change the contract revision. Changing `wotversion`, `versionid` or `dataschema` alone does not change it either; a change to the payload contract still requires a new revision. This revision is independent of a TD's `version.instance` and a TM's `version.model`. The publication profile or binding defines the payload mapping and its contract revision; these rules do not change WoT Resource identity, Version assignment, or compatibility policy.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A reference MAY carry a minimum SemVer, called its floor, but MUST NOT carry a version range. `tm:minVersion` is a member of `tm:extends` or `tm:submodel` links and a sibling of `tm:ref`. `td:minVersion` is a member of `td:extends` or `td:subthing` links and a sibling of `td:ref`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A floor MUST be a SemVer 2.0.0 string without build metadata and within Core's 128-character [id limit][Core id constraints]. It MUST NOT have the generated `0.0.0-N` form. Invalid syntax or a generated floor MUST produce `invalid-version`. `td:minVersion` on a TM reference and `tm:minVersion` on a TD-to-TD reference MUST produce `invalid-floor`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with exactly one `rel: "type"` link, its `version.model`, when present, is the implicit floor of that link. If the link also has an explicit `tm:minVersion`, the greater value by SemVer precedence is the effective floor. An explicit lower value MUST NOT weaken the implicit floor. If only one floor is present, that floor applies.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with several type links and `version.model`, every type link MUST carry its own `tm:minVersion`. Otherwise, resolution MUST fail as `ambiguous-floor`, including when resolving a different, fully specified link. When every link has a floor, each link MUST use the greater of its own floor and `version.model`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For several type links without `version.model`, each link uses its own floor if present. An omitted floor MUST NOT produce `ambiguous-floor`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A non-SemVer implicit floor MUST produce `invalid-version`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A `tm:ref` or `td:ref` is document-local when its URI-reference, resolved against the containing document's base URI and with its fragment removed, identifies that same document. A document-local reference targets the containing revision being processed, not a Resource lookup. When it carries a floor, the resolver MUST compare the floor with that revision's `version.model` for `tm:ref` or `version.instance` for `td:ref`. A `td:ref` floor also applies the TD major cap. A missing authored version, or one below the floor or outside the cap, MUST produce `unsatisfied`. An invalid authored version MUST produce `invalid-version`. The resolver MUST NOT select another Version of the containing Resource to satisfy a local reference.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A resolver MUST return `(wotid, versionid, contentdigest, origin)`, where `origin` identifies the registry from which the stored bytes were obtained and `contentdigest` is the digest of those bytes. A Consumer MAY retain this tuple outside the document and pass either a digest pin or a `versionid` pin on a subsequent resolution. A request MUST contain at most one kind of pin. Documents MUST NOT carry registry version pins or digest pins. A floor is a compatibility requirement, not a pin. Authored references and document bytes MUST remain portable between registries.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.2. Resolver Algorithm

requirements.text: The resolver MUST apply these steps in order:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.2. Resolver Algorithm

requirements.text: 1. Find the Resource whose `wotid` equals the reference target. If none exists, fail as `not-found`. A deprecated Resource is eligible and MUST NOT be replaced automatically by its `deprecated.alternative`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: A WoT publication that claims domain-complete closure MUST include the `http://opcfoundation.org/UA/WoT-Binding/publication-closure/1` extension as a REQUIRED manifest extension. Its document format is `wot-publication-closure/1`, as defined by the [closure schema](schemas/publication-closure.schema.json). The extension does not change the authored WoT documents or their reference semantics.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: Each `entries` item, binding `source` and binding `target` MUST be an exact Version XID in the captured Registry view. A target MUST identify one associated Version document, not a Resource XID, default-Version alias, WoT identifier or URL. The captured Registry model determines the target Resource's kind. A Consumer MUST validate that kind and target identity against the source occurrence using the mapping defined for that reference kind. The closure document does not add a target-kind field or authorize a different selection rule. If no such mapping is defined, the Consumer MUST reject the binding.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: A producer MUST derive the closure from the captured source document bytes, not from the binding list. Each external reference occurrence in the closure MUST have exactly one binding to its exact target Version. The binding's `source`, `pointer`, `operator` and `href` MUST identify that occurrence and preserve its authored reference. A Consumer MUST verify those values against the captured source bytes and MUST NOT resolve a missing binding against a live Registry, select a default Version, or replace the target with a newer Version.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: The extension alone therefore does not establish WoT-complete closure. A producer MUST NOT claim that completeness unless it can identify and validate every in-scope reference under a defined mapping. A Consumer MUST reject a closure whose scope or target mapping it cannot validate. The existing schema and sample check the descriptor's shape, not these missing semantic mappings.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.2. Thing Description to Thing Description

requirements.text: A TD-to-TD reference selects a Version of the target `thingdescription` Resource using its `wotid` and SemVer `versionid`, derived from the target `version.instance` as specified in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning). For `td:extends`, `td:subthing` and `td:ref`, `td:minVersion` is an OPTIONAL floor. A floor limits the target Version to `[floor, (major + 1).0.0)`. Without a floor, resolution selects the highest eligible Version overall and can cross major versions. The referencing TD's `version.instance` and `version.model` do not supply an implicit floor.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: - A registry MUST accept and serve a valid TD whose affordances are all declared in one document, with no grouping construct of any kind.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: - A registry MUST NOT require an affordance to belong to a group in order to be stored, retrieved, or referenced.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: Proposals to sub-divide a large TD's affordances, such as a `td:submodel` grouping member, are being discussed in the W3C WoT community. Were such a mechanism to be standardized, a WoT Registry would store a TD that uses it exactly as it stores any other TD, since the grouping is a member of the document rather than of the registry model. Support is OPTIONAL. A registry that does not understand the mechanism MUST still store and serve the document unchanged, per [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: Documents authored outside the Registry routinely contain no grouping construct. They MUST remain fully supported.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Implementations are expected to use authentication and authorization appropriate to the application domain and deployment environment. Those mechanisms MAY include OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, API keys or other options appropriate to the use case.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Operators of a WoT Registry SHOULD be aware that Thing Descriptions can expose detailed information about deployed devices, including network locations, operational endpoints, and security schemes. The [WoT Security and Privacy Considerations][WoT-Security] document gives additional guidance.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: A Consumer or Registry that resolves them SHOULD confine resolution to the Registry and its declared federation links. Where a deployment has to dereference an authored URL it SHOULD:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: The same `wotid` MAY appear in more than one Group ([Section 5.3](#53-lookup)). A writer with access to any Group within a Registry-wide query's scope can therefore publish a document carrying another party's `wotid` and claims of high `maturity`/`standardsbody` status. A Consumer selecting on those attributes alone would compose the attacker's Thing Model and bind its affordances to that model's endpoints.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Selection MUST therefore be scoped to writers the Consumer already trusts.
